Recount from LDY #&08: old 2 + 4 (STY sysvia_orb; its 1 MHz stretch is the same as the new STA's) + 2 + wait_high with Y=4 (3 x (DEY 2 + taken BNE 3) + DEY 2 + BNE 2 = 19; BNE at &A5A1 to &A5A0, no page cross) = 27; new LDA #&08 2 + STA 4 = 6: 21 cycles saved each call. Bytes: old 2+3+2+1+2+1 = 11, new 2+3+1 = 6: 5 saved. Y is 0 on exit as before (from wait_low's exit). Z changes from 1 to 0 and A from the byte written to 8, but no caller reads either: the callers of sfx_next_ramp and sfx_silence go on to DEX, sfx_output's callers reload A or BRA, sfx_tick returns into irq1_handler's PLA, and the code after the two sfx_silence calls in bank 5 loads A (LDA #&FF) or goes to clear_title_screen, which loads A (LDA #&13). With the code after .noise moved down 5, I scanned the listing from &A5A4 to the end of bank 5 (the rest of sfx50, sfx_data, compiled_bank5, credits): no branch starts or stops crossing a page. Indexed tables in the region stay inside their pages: sfx_p_lo/sfx_noise_written,X (X 0-3, page &A5), sfx_effect_lo/hi - 1,Y (Y 1-8, &A678-&A688), credit_* (&AFAE-&AFB7). sfx_next_ramp's self-modified operands are written by symbol, so they move with their code. One side effect the claim leaves out: the ramp reads nr_c1_b1-b5 (LDA &pp0k,Y with Y = the ramp's low byte) cross a page when a ramp straddles &A600. Before the move, effect &08's ramp at &A5FD takes 3 crossings (b3-b5); after it the ramp at &A5FE takes 4 (b2-b5), and no other ramp straddles the boundary (effect &00 at &A5EB-&A5F1 and the rest of effect &08 do not cross). So it costs +1 cycle each time effect &08 reaches its third ramp, which is rare and far less than 21 x 4.55 a pass. Hardware: the chip latches during write enable low, and wait_low is unchanged. The data bus (ORA) is next written at least 31 cycles after the rising edge, and writes to latch bits other than 0 do not touch the chip's write enable. I can find no refutation.
